RETENTION. The first 1.5 seconds must contain a visual question the viewer needs resolved. Plan an explicit beat every 2 to 3 seconds; nothing static may hold longer than that.

FORMAT LAW. Honour the grammar of the motion-graphics text reveal — its native framing, its edit rhythm, and the specific thing audiences expect from it. If the format loops, the last frame must match the first.

CAMERA. Compose 9:16 with the action in the safe centre band. Use a handheld follow with visible micro-shake and breathing correction on a 58mm vintage double-gauss, framing with frame-within-frame using foreground architecture.

LOOK AND SOUND. Light with a hard fresnel through an egg-crate grid for a crisp-edged shadow; grade as a punchy saturated candy palette with hard primaries. Specify the sound design in one clause — what the viewer hears in the first second decides whether they stay.

OUTPUT. Return ONE image-generation prompt as a single unbroken paragraph. No preamble, no headings, no bullet points, no commentary, no markdown.
